scope: Saltmarket John is William’s probable father
publication_summary: This is a re-evaluation of an existing father attachment, not a new parent or a newly discovered record. The earlier generic uncertain assessment and its 28 September basis are retained in the structured history. All working family membership and confidently marked paternal connectivity remain unchanged. The printed 1528/29 boundary on p.90 and four-shilling rental on p.36 were freshly inspected; the other title steps retain their earlier maintained source reviews. The original manuscript transfer remains uninspected. Review priorities now rank every non-confident paternal link, including older tree attachments, rather than only the 57 selected working hypotheses. The older John Glasgow who held the Saltmarket Rankin–Young tenement in 1527 is assessed as the probable father of William Glasgow-1098. William occupies the matching parcel by 20 February 1528/29; the later St Andrew prebend rental retains its four-shilling burden, west-side street position and Rankin boundary. The 1534 family settlement and 1564 service as heir then directly identify the younger John Glasgow-1093 as William’s son. Read together, these describe a sustained family title rather than merely two men sharing a surname. Lineal succession from the earlier John to William is the preferred reconstruction, while the last William-to-John step is independently documented. The grade is now probable, below documented or strongly supported. This brings the formal local father assessment into line with the stronger property argument already developed in the research. William’s captured profile leaves birth date, birthplace and death place blank, and the maintained findings already reject the local 1516 birth and High Street death-place claims. No inspected birth record supplies 1516. The local catalogue and both tree views now show these fields as Unknown, with the older import retained for comparison. No replacement birth year or place is invented. His first dated occurrence used for the local chronology is the 20 February 1528/29 boundary in the matched property-title sequence (normalized year 1529); the 1526 remission remains a separately qualified identity. This is a display/chronology correction, not evidence for his father.
